title: Colour picker
slide_intent: Teach designers to choose an exhibition accent in relation to its lead artwork. A background can draw a connection to the subject while giving the title enough contrast to read.
strategic_value: Sheffield Museums can give successive exhibitions distinct identities while the gallery wordmark and museum seal keep the host recognizable.
demonstration: An artwork detail, an eyedropper and a turquoise swatch sit in sequence beneath a finished exhibition graphic. In the graphic, the turquoise field carries black type beside the lead image.
practical_value: Test the proposed accent behind the exhibition title. Keep it if the title reads clearly and the composition improves on white, black or a core palette color.

content_islands.name: Page heading
content_islands.spec: Set the section number and Colour palette at upper left with the printed folio at upper right. Place the Colour picker title beneath the section label.

content_islands.name: Selection instructions
content_islands.spec: Use a narrow left column. Introduce the exhibition-specific option, then number the steps for choosing the image, sampling or complementing it, adjusting readability and comparing against the core palette.

content_islands.name: Exhibition graphic
content_islands.spec: Give the wider upper field to the completed Not Without My Ghosts graphic. Set the gallery mark, title and dates on turquoise, with the artwork on the right.

content_islands.name: Color selection sequence
content_islands.spec: Below the graphic, align a square detail from the artwork, a small eyedropper and a large circular accent swatch. Join them with right-pointing arrows so the reader can trace the choice.

ingredient.name: Exhibition accent
ingredient.role: Connect the exhibition graphics to the work on show. On this poster, the turquoise field carries the title beside the painting.
ingredient.application: Choose one prominent hue from the lead artwork, or one that complements it. Avoid a color too close to the existing palette. Adjust tone or vibrancy for legibility and try it as a background or on graphic elements.
ingredient.scope: An optional choice for one exhibition. The example’s turquoise belongs to Not Without My Ghosts; another exhibition starts with its own lead image.

reference_purposes.Intent: The text says exhibition accents provide variety and flexibility so materials suit their subject matter.
reference_purposes.Expression: The finished Not Without My Ghosts graphic demonstrates a turquoise title field beside its lead artwork.
reference_purposes.Application: The numbered sequence teaches sampling or complementing a lead image, adjusting legibility and applying the accent.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The custom color is optional, limited to exhibitions and must not be too close to an existing palette color.
